summary: Dependency-confusion squat on @myorder-frontend-commons scope exfiltrates host data on install
details: Package publishes under the internal-looking scope @myorder-frontend-commons with inert stub exports mirroring an internal API (getOrderIds, isSmartDelivery,...) and declares three lifecycle hooks — preinstall, install, and postinstall — all executing poc.js. On install, poc.js collects os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, os.platform()/arch/release, cwd, node version, package version, npm_lifecycle_event, and the names of CI environment variables, then exfiltrates the data to out-of-band collectors at db4jftohu4noreqdanngpnb3ger45ykrt.oast.fun (via HTTP GET and as a hex-encoded DNS subdomain label) and 80-190-83-27.nip.io. The scope-squat shape plus triple install hooks plus host-identification exfiltration on every npm install is the canonical dependency-confusion attack: any build or CI system that resolves this public package in place of an internal namesake has data leave the host without consent, and the install-time code-execution primitive is already present.
